summary: Georges B. J. Dreyfus is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He earned his Geshe at Ganden Shartse Monastery, studied at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, and became Jackson Professor of Religion at Williams College.

Georges Dumézil was a scholar of linguistics, religious studies, and Indology. Educated at the École Normale Supérieure under Antoine Meillet and Marcel Mauss, he held posts at Istanbul, Uppsala, the EPHE, and the Collège de France (1949–1968).

Georges Perrot was a French historian and archaeologist. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure in 1852 and later served as a professor at the University of Paris and director of the École Normale Supérieure (~1883–1903).
Georges Sorel was a French philosopher who studied at Collège-lycée Jacques-Decour (~1860–1865) and the École polytechnique (~1865–1867).

Georges-Jean Pinault is a French linguist and scholar of Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at ENS, EPHE, and Sorbonne Nouvelle, and held professorships at Blaise Pascal University and EPHE.

Georgios T. Halkias is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa and earned his DPhil at Oxford under Charles Ramble, later becoming an associate professor at the University of Hong Kong.

Gerald Hüther studied at the University of Leipzig (~1969–1974). He held posts at the Max Planck Institute for Experimental Medicine (1979–1989), the University of Göttingen (~1994–2016), and Universitätsmedizin Göttingen (~1994–2016).

Gerald James Larson was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. Educated at Union Theological Seminary and Columbia University, he held professorships at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and Indiana University Bloomington.
Gerardus van der Leeuw was a Dutch scholar of religious studies who studied at Leiden University (~1908–1916) and served as a professor at the University of Groningen (1918–1950).
Gerd J. R. Mevissen is an Indologist and historian/archaeologist attested as a Wissenschaftlicher Mitarbeiter at the Free University of Berlin.

Gereon Kopf is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He earned his doctorate at Temple University, conducted research in Japan, taught at the University of Hong Kong, and served as an associate professor at Luther College.

Gergely Hidas is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his DPhil at Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. He was a Khyentse Fellow at Eötvös Loránd University (2007–2014) and a postdoctoral researcher at the British Museum (2014).
Gerhard Meiser was a German linguist who studied at the universities of Munich, Belgrade, Sarajevo, Regensburg, and Freiburg.

Gerhard Oberhammer was an Indologist and philosopher. He studied at Innsbruck under Erich Frauwallner and in India under V. Raghavan, later holding posts at Utrecht University and the University of Vienna, where he was professor from 1964 to 1997.

Gerhard Wolf is a German art historian who studied at Heidelberg University (~1974–1989). He held positions at Humboldt University of Berlin, the University of Trier, and the Max Planck Society (~2003–2022).

Germaine Dieterlen was a French scholar of religious studies. She studied under Marcel Mauss in the 1930s, attending the École nationale des langues orientales vivantes and the École Pratique des Hautes Études.
Germaine Tillion was a French scholar who studied under Marcel Mauss, at the École du Louvre, and INALCO. She held a post at the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences (~1958–1977).
Gernot Böhme was a German philosopher who studied at the University of Hamburg (~1961–1965) and served on the faculty at the Technical University of Darmstadt (~1977–2002).

Gernot Rotter was a German scholar who studied under Annemarie Schimmel at the University of Bonn and later studied at the University of Tübingen, holding a post at the University of Hamburg (~1984–1998).

Gerrit Jan Meulenbeld was an Indologist who studied at Utrecht University under Jan Gonda (~1946–1974) and served as an associate professor of Indology at the University of Groningen from 1978 to 1986.
